the library under requiem and req

swift-http-files

six libraries, layered — a target links only what it needs
everything is a region or a transformer; there is no engine
position is the contract: a signer placed after resolve sees the resolved request
the result document is the file — valid .http at every step
req is one of http.vet's seven graded lanes, from source, no special standing

code chart · u+2800–28ff · 256/256

Base256

a byte given a face — one braille cell per byte
left column dots 1 2 3 7 = high nibble · right column dots 4 5 6 8 = low
read top to bottom, most significant first
a fixed permutation of the block, not 0x2800 + byte
foundation-free core · consumed by blob and Signs & Tokens
the four lit corners are the anchors — 00 · 0F · F0 · FF

public · mit · tag 1.0.0

hmac.sh/eC1hbXo/prod/data/hmac

/ eC1hbXokey ← base64url · 782d616d7a · "x-amz" · 5 B
/ prodHr0zaEY84FmNOR8y0AQon-R2JyHG32v-NyCXwFI3P70
/ data6nNiv_5Gd2GXfN4vgQV0AoUmLpliOGGuuf4_vgevjgk
/ hmac → 303 locationLkm2jwu--qxw3F3hUpvsdKxfJFOzrHix-dhkqMuIcPo 
$ K=$(printf x-amz | xxd -p -c256)
$ for D in prod data hmac; do K=$(printf %s "$D" \
    | openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC -macopt hexkey:$K \
    -binary | xxd -p -c256); done
$ printf %s "$K" | xxd -r -p | base64 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='

hmac.sh

every slash is one hmac-sha256 round — the digest keys the next
the redirect target is itself a valid key: /Lkm2jwu…/x-amz.dev → /jbi9t5al…
key ≤ 128 bytes decoded · segment ≤ 128 chars · cache-control no-store
